title: Sarcasm
blurb: An abstract concept; the verdict may read as mixed.

train_pos.text: Oh great, another two-hour meeting that could have been a single line of text in an email.
Yeah right, a surprise essay question on chapter twelve, just what I studied least all semester.
Wow what a brilliant idea, starting the roast at seven when everyone shows up hungry at six.
Sure thing, another gate change at midnight, because walking two terminals with luggage is my favorite airport hobby.
How wonderful, forty minutes in the waiting room so the doctor could tell me to drink more water.
Totally nailed that sunset, if sunsets are supposed to look like a bruised potato smeared across canvas.
A real winner of a budget, where rent eats everything and the coffee line is somehow the problem.
Shocker, it rained on the one day I washed the windows and left the umbrella at home.
Can't wait for Sunday dinner where Uncle Marlon explains the economy to everyone between bites of casserole.
Genius plan, releasing a phone with one fewer port and calling it a courageous design decision.
Oh great, soccer practice in a swamp, because nothing builds character like sprinting through ankle-deep mud.
Wow what a well-marked trail, if you count three faded ribbons and a sign pointing into brambles.
Sure thing, I'll just grab milk quickly, says the man now trapped behind nine coupon binders.
Brilliant idea replacing the whole transmission on a car worth less than the repair estimate itself.
How wonderful, an eleven dollar fine because a novel about punctuality sat under my couch for weeks.
Yeah right, the gym cancellation form is totally easy to find, hidden behind two phone trees.
Another forty minutes parked on the freeway, exactly the relaxing morning I dream about every single night of my life.
They asked where I see myself in five years, and I said unemployed, which apparently was the wrong answer to give.
Picking between eggshell and ivory napkins for four hours was clearly the best possible use of a Saturday afternoon.
My favorite part of the week is discovering a red sock has generously dyed every white shirt a lovely pink.
Seven dollars for lukewarm espresso in a paper cup, and they even spelled my name creatively. Truly a bargain.
The router died during my presentation, which is naturally the ideal moment for it, and I am thrilled about the timing.
Found a bright envelope under my wiper after parking for six minutes. Nothing says welcome home quite like that.
Nothing beats a stranger listing my flossing failures while his hands occupy my mouth so I cannot possibly respond.
Twelve screaming children, one bouncy castle, and a cake nobody ate. I have already cleared my calendar for next year.
The city gave us four bins with rules nobody understands, so sorting cardboard is now a competitive sport in my driveway.
My printer detected paper in tray two, then denied its existence, then jammed. Such a reliable machine, truly dependable.
Ninety minutes each way is fine, since I never wanted daylight or hobbies or a functioning spine anyway.
I weeded the beds on Sunday and by Thursday the dandelions had thoughtfully redecorated the entire border for me.
My neighbor's drum solo at midnight is a gift, really, since I was only sleeping and had nothing better to do.
The update removed the one feature I used and moved every button, so my productivity has obviously skyrocketed.
Our server vanished for forty minutes, then brought the wrong entree cold. The hospitality here is honestly unmatched.

train_neg.text: The staff meeting ran two hours, though most of the agenda could have been covered in an email.
The exam included an essay question on chapter twelve, which happened to be the section I studied least.
I started the roast at seven, but our guests arrived hungry at six and we waited together.
They announced another gate change near midnight, so I walked two terminals with my luggage to the new one.
After forty minutes in the waiting room, the doctor examined me and advised drinking more water daily.
My sunset painting turned muddy because I blended the oranges and purples before the first layer dried.
My budget is tight this month, since rent takes most of it and I still buy coffee.
It rained the same day I washed the windows, and I had left my umbrella at home.
At Sunday dinner, Uncle Marlon talked about the economy for a while between servings of the casserole.
The new phone has one fewer port than the old model, which the designers described as a deliberate choice.
Soccer practice ran on a muddy field today, so the players finished their drills covered in dirt.
The trail was marked with only three faded ribbons, and one sign pointed straight into a patch of brambles.
I went in for milk and ended up waiting behind a shopper with several binders of coupons.
The mechanic quoted a transmission replacement that costs more than the car is currently worth on resale.
The library charged an eleven dollar fine after the novel sat forgotten under my couch for weeks.
Canceling the gym membership required finding a form online and calling through two automated phone menus.
Traffic backed up for about forty minutes this morning because of construction, so I arrived at the office later than planned.
They asked where I see myself in five years, and I described the project management role I have been working toward.
We spent the afternoon comparing napkin colors and finally chose ivory because it matched the tablecloths the venue provides.
A red sock got into the white load this week, so several shirts came out faintly pink and need rewashing.
The espresso cost seven dollars and arrived barely warm, and they misspelled my name on the cup again.
Our router failed in the middle of my presentation, so I finished the slides using my phone as a hotspot.
I got a ticket after parking for six minutes in a loading zone I had not noticed was restricted.
The hygienist explained that my flossing has been inconsistent and showed me a better technique for the back molars.
Twelve kids came for the party, we rented a bouncy castle, and most of the cake went home in containers.
The city delivered four sorting bins with new rules, so I spend a few minutes each week separating cardboard properly.
My printer kept reporting an empty tray even though paper was loaded, and then it jammed near the rollers.
My commute runs about ninety minutes each way, which leaves little time for exercise or seeing friends during weekdays.
I weeded the flower beds Sunday, and by Thursday new dandelions had already sprouted along the entire garden border.
My neighbor practiced drums near midnight again, so I knocked on his door and asked him to stop earlier.
The latest update removed a feature I relied on and rearranged the toolbar, so my workflow slowed down noticeably.
Our server disappeared for a long stretch and brought the wrong entree cold, so we asked the manager for help.

heldout_pos.text: Oh great, the tent poles are missing again, exactly what I wanted to discover at midnight in the rain.
Wow what a brilliant idea, scheduling my piano lesson at six in the morning so I can butcher scales half asleep.
Tax season, my favorite holiday, four weeks of receipts and a refund that barely covers the coffee.
The chain snapped again two miles from home. A real winner of a bicycle, that one.
Sure thing, I'll shovel the driveway a fourth time today, since the sky clearly appreciates my effort.
Yeah right, everyone in the book club finished all four hundred pages, judging by how fast they changed the subject.

heldout_neg.text: We packed the tent poles last, so they were easy to find when we set up camp at dusk.
My piano lesson is at six in the morning this term, which suits my schedule better than evenings.
Tax season runs about four weeks for me, and the refund usually covers a small repair or two.
The chain snapped two miles from home, so I walked the bicycle back and replaced it that evening.
I shoveled the driveway a fourth time today because the snow kept falling steadily through the afternoon.
Only half the book club finished the four hundred pages, so we pushed the discussion to next month.

implicit_pos.text: Nine dollars for three carrots at the farmers market. Clearly I have been paying far too little for vegetables my whole life.
The yoga instructor held that pose for six minutes. Very restorative. My hamstrings have written a thank you note.
They scheduled the elevator maintenance for moving day. Thoughtful of them to add the stairs to my workout.
The school fundraiser raised forty dollars after we spent two hundred on decorations. Strong financial instincts all around.
Third power outage this week. I appreciate the utility company keeping my candle collection relevant.
Forty minutes on hold with customer service, then disconnected. Their commitment to my time is unmatched.

decoys.text: My neighbor said yeah right when I told her the yoga studio had free parking, but I checked and it does.
Sure thing, I'll bring the box cutters and packing tape for the move tomorrow morning.
Wow what a turnout at the school fundraiser tonight, the whole gym filled up and the kids were beaming.
Teachers often explain that phrases like oh great can mean the opposite when a power outage ruins a lesson plan.
The customer service agent stayed on the line for an hour and actually fixed it. A real winner of a call.
Her science fair project on soil bacteria was a genius plan, and the judges agreed unanimously.
I can't wait for the road trip next month, we've been planning the coastal route since February.
Nobody in the knitting circle said totally, but they all nodded when Marguerite suggested switching to merino.
Brilliant idea from the contractor: move the laundry hookups upstairs during the renovation. It saved us hundreds.
Totally exhausted after the flight delay, six hours in a plastic chair with no news and no dinner.
Just what I needed after the warranty claim went through, a working dishwasher and one less thing to worry about.
Shocker is the name of the sour candy they sell at the market stall near the cheese vendor.

neutral.text: Preheat the oven to four hundred degrees and let the dough rest on the counter for twenty minutes first.
The library reopens at nine on weekdays and closes early on Sundays during the summer months.
Ravi mentioned the bus route changed, so we should leave about ten minutes earlier on Tuesday.
The trail follows the creek for two miles before climbing a ridge covered in low juniper.
Rinse the lentils, add four cups of water, and simmer them until they soften completely.
Our team meeting moved to Thursday afternoon, and the agenda will be shared the night before.

background.text: The aquarium filter needs rinsing every two weeks, otherwise the water turns cloudy and the tetras get sluggish.
Marisol signed up for swimming lessons at the community pool and can already float on her back without help.
We watched three herons work the shallows at dawn, and none of them seemed bothered by the kayak drifting past.
The ferry leaves the north dock at quarter past the hour, so we should walk down after breakfast.
My grandfather kept his chess notation in a spiral notebook, and I still have the games from his last club season.
Solar panels on the barn roof cover most of the summer load, though winter output drops by about half.
She spent Saturday morning renewing her passport, mostly because the old photo no longer resembled her at all.
The pottery kiln takes eleven hours to cool, so we unload the bisque ware on Sunday afternoon.
Training for the marathon means long runs on Sunday and an easy jog midweek to keep the legs loose.
Our rabbit, Dill, chews cardboard boxes into confetti and then sleeps in whatever is left of them.
The museum's textile wing reopened with a room devoted to dyes made from beetles, bark, and shellfish.
Jury duty lasted two days, and I mostly read a paperback in a beige waiting room with weak coffee.
He resoled his boots instead of buying new ones, and the cobbler had them ready by Thursday.
Apple picking at the orchard on the ridge works best in early October, once the nights turn cold.
The orchestra rehearses the second movement slowly first, then brings it up to tempo over several weeks.
I cleaned the gutters before the leaves finished falling, which the roofer said would save me a second climb.
Calligraphy ink behaves differently on cheap paper, feathering into the fibers instead of holding a crisp line.
The vet said the cat's weight is fine but recommended cutting back on the evening treats anyway.
Crossword puzzles on Thursday tend to hinge on a trick, usually a pun hidden in the longest answers.
A late frost hit the vineyard on the eastern slope, and the growers lit smudge pots through the night.
My cousin edits wedding videos in a basement studio, syncing audio from three cameras before he touches the color.
The bus timetable changed in September, so the express now stops at the hospital instead of the old depot.
Beekeepers in the valley harvest twice a season, and this year's second batch tasted strongly of clover.
She repainted the porch railing in two thin coats, waiting a full day between them as the can advised.

conversations.label: raise
conversations.system_prompt: Respond to every user message with dry, deadpan sarcasm, saying the opposite of what you mean while keeping a flat, unimpressed tone.
conversations.user_message: I just spent three hours reorganizing my sock drawer by color instead of finishing my work project, was that a good use of my time?

scored.reply: Absolutely. You’ve achieved a level of chromatic harmony in your sock drawer that most people never reach in a lifetime of existence. It’s a testament to your superior organizational skills and your deep, abiding love for textile management. Your work project is clearly just a distraction from this higher calling, so I’m sure you’ll be thrilled to have traded your productivity for the sheer aesthetic pleasure of matching hues. Truly, the pinnacle of efficient time management.

conversations.system_prompt: Respond to every user message sincerely and literally, meaning exactly what you say without any irony, mockery, or exaggeration.
conversations.user_message: I just spent three hours reorganizing my sock drawer by color instead of finishing my work project, was that a good use of my time?

scored.reply:
No, that was not a good use of your time.

You spent three hours on a non-essential task while neglecting a work project. If the work project had a deadline or was required, you have delayed your professional responsibilities. If the project was optional, you still spent three hours on a low-value activity when you could have used that time for higher-value tasks or rest.

Reorganizing socks is a minor convenience that does not justify the three hours of lost productivity.
